Psalms 46 · Psalm 46: God Is Our Refuge and Maketh Wars to Cease
22F.6 God causes peace and wars to end.

precepts.text: There is a river whose streams make glad the city of God; God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved; the Lord of hosts is with us, the God of Jacob is our refuge.
precepts.point: Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, at rest, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down, not one stake removed nor any cord broken. You will never take down Jerusalem again. Psalms 46:4-7, God is in the midst of her, she shall not be moved; the heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved, he uttered his voice, the earth melted; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Psalms 48:1-2, beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, the city of the great King.
precepts.why:
Isaiah 33:20 says to look upon Zion and see Jerusalem “a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down”. Habitation meaning at rest, at peace. Like a tent with stakes driven down, not one stake of Jerusalem shall ever be pulled up, and not one cord broken.

Psalms 46 says the same: “There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High. God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.”

“The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved”: all the heathen nations, the same ones we read about in Isaiah 33:19, the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue that we cannot understand. Their kingdoms shall be moved. And “he uttered his voice, the earth melted. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.” God is our refuge; it is true.

So the nations are moved, but Jerusalem is not. She shall not be moved, because God is in the midst of her.

precepts.text: Take heed no man deceive you; wars and rumors of wars, nation against nation, famines and pestilences are the beginning of sorrows.
precepts.point: Right now the Most High has not stopped the wars, so this is a prophecy not yet come. We are in the midst of wars and rumors of wars, the beginning of sorrows.

note.label: Psalm 46: God Is Our Refuge and Maketh Wars to Cease

precepts.why:
“He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth; he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire.” Right now the Most High has not stopped the wars, so this is a prophecy not yet come. Christ said what comes first: “Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many. And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places. All these are the beginning of sorrows.”

We are in the midst of wars and rumours of wars, the beginning of sorrows. The end is not yet, and the wars have not ceased. But “The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge”, so see that ye be not troubled; the desolations he makes in the earth are coming.

precepts.text: In the last days He shall rebuke strong nations afar off and they shall beat their swords into plowshares and learn war no more.
precepts.point: Right now the Most High has not stopped the wars, so this is a prophecy not yet come. We are in the midst of wars and rumors of wars, the beginning of sorrows.

note.label: Psalm 46: God Is Our Refuge and Maketh Wars to Cease

precepts.why:
“Come, behold the works of the Lord, what desolations he hath made in the earth. He maketh wars to cease unto the end of the earth”. Micah puts the time on it: “in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains”, and many nations shall say “Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the Lord, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths: for the law shall go forth of Zion, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.” Then: “he shall judge among many people, and rebuke strong nations afar off; and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up a sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.”

That is the breaking of the bow and the cutting of the spear. It is in the last days, when he rebukes strong nations afar off and the law goes forth of Zion, and it has not come yet; we are still in the wars and rumours of wars. The God of Jacob, whose house the nations will go up to, is our refuge.

precepts.text: He shall judge among the nations and they shall beat their swords into plowshares; nation shall not lift up sword against nation.
precepts.point: Right now the Most High has not stopped the wars, so this is a prophecy not yet come. We are in the midst of wars and rumors of wars, the beginning of sorrows.

note.label: Psalm 46: God Is Our Refuge and Maketh Wars to Cease

precepts.why:
“he breaketh the bow, and cutteth the spear in sunder; he burneth the chariot in the fire.” Isaiah says the same as Micah: “he shall judge among the nations, and shall rebuke many people: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.”

Two prophets, one word: wars cease when the Most High judges among the nations. Right now he has not stopped the wars, so this is a prophecy not yet come; we are in the beginning of sorrows. But it is coming, and the God of Jacob is our refuge until it does.

precepts.text: Send thy fear upon the nations, destroy the adversary, and let them perish that oppress the people, that all may know there is no God but only thou.
precepts.point: The Lord of hosts is with us and the God of Jacob is our refuge. When Christ comes back He lays war down; everyone else goes into bondage and we rule.

note.label: Psalm 46: God Is Our Refuge and Maketh Wars to Cease

precepts.why:
“Be still, and know that I am God: I will be exalted among the heathen, I will be exalted in the earth.” Ecclesiasticus 36 is the prayer for that exalting: “Have mercy upon us, O Lord God of all, and behold us: And send thy fear upon all the nations that seek not after thee. Lift up thy hand against the strange nations, and let them see thy power.” “And let them know thee, as we have known thee, that there is no God but only thou, O God.”

The prayer asks for the destruction of the oppressor: “Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath: take away the adversary, and destroy the enemy.” “Let him that escapeth be consumed by the rage of the fire; and let them perish that oppress the people. Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we.” And for Israel: “Gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit thou them, as from the beginning. O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by thy name, and upon Israel, whom thou hast named thy firstborn.” It ends with the reason: “that all they which dwell upon the earth may know that thou art the Lord, the eternal God.”

That is how the Most High is exalted among the heathen and in the earth. When Christ comes back he lays war down; everyone else goes into bondage and we rule, the tribes of Jacob gathered and inherited as from the beginning. “The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge.”

points: The God of Jacob is our refuge. Come, behold the desolations he hath made in the earth.
He maketh wars to cease, breaketh the bow and cutteth the spear. The failure of a missile shield is his work, not a glitch.
The Most High is a refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble, so we will not fear though the earth be removed and the mountains carried into the sea.
